question: I need to launch a new analytics dashboard project that includes data processing from our customer CSV files, log analysis from our application logs, and visualization components. Can you help me structure the major milestones and break them down into manageable tasks, making sure we don't have any tasks that are too complex to execute?
answer:
Done. Your **Analytics Dashboard** project is now fully structured — 48 tasks across 6 milestones, all connected by dependencies, with no oversize leaf work items.

## Milestone structure

| # | Milestone | Children | Total est. |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Foundation & Data Platform Setup | 5 tasks | 60h |
| M2 | Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing | 7 tasks | 80h |
| M3 | Application Log Analysis | 11 tasks | 70h |
| M4 | Metrics API & Query Layer | 6 tasks | 60h |
| M5 | Visualization & Dashboard Frontend | 6 tasks | 80h |
| M6 | Quality, Observability & Launch | 7 tasks | 70h |

## How each section breaks down

**M1 – Foundation:** repo scaffold → local container stack → storage schema/migrations → shared data contracts → synthetic CSV + log fixtures. Everything downstream depends on the schema and contract tasks, so those are wired as blockers.

**M2 – CSV pipeline:** upload/landing zone → streaming parser with encoding + column mapping → validation rules engine → cleaning/normalization → quarantine & validation report → idempotent loader → 100k-row load test. It's a clean linear chain: parser → validation → transforms → loader → load test.

**M3 – Log pipeline:** format inventory → line parser → multi-line/stack-trace grouping → canonical normalization → rollups. The two heaviest pieces were split into a second level (`Rollup A`/`Rollup B`, `Clustering A`/`Clustering B`), as was scheduling/freshness tracking.

**M4 – API:** scaffolding → auth/RBAC → customer endpoints → log-health endpoints → ingestion/data-quality endpoints → filtering/pagination/caching/OpenAPI.

**M5 – Frontend:** shell + typed API client → chart component library → URL-synced filter bar → two dashboard views (customer analytics, app health) → responsiveness/accessibility. Both views depend on the chart library, the filter bar, *and* the corresponding M4 endpoints.

**M6 – Launch:** unit tests → integration/e2e → CI/CD → monitoring/alerting → performance validation → docs/runbook → pilot + GA sign-off (the final task gates on all of the above).

## Complexity check
I ran complexity analysis twice. The first pass flagged two leaf tasks at 6/10 — `Rollup metrics` and `Error signature clustering` — so I **split both into two 4–5/10 children**. I then shortened two overly long task names the analyzer also flagged. **Every executable leaf task now sits at complexity 5 or below** (typically 7–12h each).

The six milestones still report 6–7/10, but they are deliberately *containers* — their complexity is a roll-up of children, not a unit of work. I annotated each milestone's description to make that explicit, so no one picks one up as a single ticket.

## Suggested starting point
The recommender points at **Repo scaffold & developer tooling** (8h, complexity 3) and **Shared data contracts & canonical field spec** (10h) as unblocked. I'd start with the scaffold plus the data contracts in parallel — the contract spec unblocks the CSV parser and API scaffolding, so it's the highest-leverage early task.

One thing worth deciding before work begins: I assumed a **5-minute log rollup freshness target** and a **REST API**. If you need sub-minute freshness or prefer GraphQL, tell me and I'll adjust the M3/M4 task scopes and their downstream dependencies.
